results.text:
Combined, the 2021 PPPs and the latest national poverty lines have contributed to higher global poverty lines (refer to table B1.1.1). They do not constitute a movement of the goalpost in poverty measurement. Rather, they reflect evolving standards of how the poorest countries measure consumption and evolving differences in the cost of living across countries as captured by an established methodology (World Bank 2025d).

TABLE B1.1.1 Revised global poverty lines Economy group Previous poverty line (2017 PPPs) Revised poverty line (2021 PPPs) Low-income economies $2.15 $3.00 Lower-middle-income economies $3.65 $4.20 Upper-middle-income economies $6.85 $8.30 Source: alfani et al. 2025.

results.text: 30 POVERTY , PROSPERITY , AND PLANET REPORT 2026 economies. At the $8.30 line, 80 percent of the poor are living in middle-income economies. A handful of large middle-income economies drive these numbers. At the $4.20 line, India, Nigeria, and Pakistan, together, account for more than a third of the global poor.
